mechanism: Relative Vigor Index: bar vigor=(CLOSE−OPEN)/(HIGH−LOW), then 4-bar weighted MovAverage of (C−O) over RangeAverage of (H−L), signal=SMA-like smooth of RVI. Sense bullish vigor when RVI>0 and RVI_signal>0 and RVI>RVI_signal; bearish when both <0 and RVI<RVI_signal. Article notes RVI works better in trending than ranging markets. Optional filter: close vs 100-EMA with RVI/signal cross.
data_needed: OHLC; iRVI(ma_period=10); buffers 0 (RVI) and 1 (signal); optional iMA(100,EMA,CLOSE).
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Any _Symbol/_Period; RVI period 10; MA 100 EMA in strategy three.
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS a close-vs-open vigor oscillator (unlike Stochastic's close-in-range) with explicit zero-half and RVI/signal alignment as a trend-favoring momentum regime sensor.
quote: By comparing the closing price to its opening level, this indicator measures the strength of the trend.

mechanism: Accelerator Oscillator AC=AO−SMA(AO,5) with AO=SMA(median,5)−SMA(median,34), median=(H+L)/2. Zero level = bulls/bears balance; AC>0 → upward continuation bias, AC<0 → downward. Strength: current AC > max of prior ~10 AC → strong acceleration; current < min → weakness/deceleration. Leading sense of momentum change before price.
data_needed: OHLC median; iAC; AC buffer length ≥11; ArrayMaximum/Minimum over prior AC; optional EMA(50) gate.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Any _Symbol/_Period; AO 5/34 embedded; SMA 5 of AO; last-ten AC extrema; EMA 50 in strategy three.
why_new_for_mis: Second-derivative momentum (acceleration of AO) as an early change sensor—distinct from first-order oscillators—for MIS regime-shift timing.
quote: the main objective of this indicator is to measure the acceleration and deceleration of the market power in both directions up or down

mechanism: Awesome Oscillator AO=SMA(median,5)−SMA(median,34), median=(H+L)/2. Zero cross: AO>0 bullish momentum control, AO<0 bearish. Strength: current AO vs average of prior 5 AO values (strong if above AVG, weak if below). Optional confirm: AO vs zero plus close vs 50-EMA.
data_needed: OHLC; iAO; AO buffer (≥6 for strength); optional iMA(50,EMA,CLOSE).
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Any _Symbol/_Period; 5 vs 34 median SMA; 5-bar AO average; EMA 50.
why_new_for_mis: Short-vs-long median-price momentum histogram as a clean bull/bear control regime and short-window strength overlay for MIS.
quote: it compares the recent momentum with the momentum of a larger time frame

mechanism: When market behavior shifts, classify automated algorithms by loss mode: (1) Lazy—trade duration blows up (e.g. max hold from hours to months) with swap drag; (2) Persistent—win-rate flips (e.g. 98%→28% winners) without notice; (3) Unstable—small parameter/spread tweak causes account blow-up or risk%→exposure% explosion. Sense market change by monitoring max trade length, consecutive losses vs backtest baseline, and parameter-fragility stress. Mitigate with global account stop-loss at 2–3× nominal DD and active/reserve capital split.
data_needed: Per-EA trade duration stats; win/loss counts vs historical expectancy; backtest DD baseline; global equity DD; parameter perturbation tests.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Generic automated EAs; example pandemic Feb 2020 regime break; multi-year backtests; account-level (not symbol-specific).
why_new_for_mis: Meta-sensor: detect market regime change through EA behavioral failure signatures (duration, expectancy flip, fragility) rather than price indicators alone.
quote: there are three different classes of algorithms when we speak about how the losses appear instead of the profit when the market is drastically changed

mechanism: Each tick: take CHART_FIRST_VISIBLE_BAR count of lows/highs; ArrayMinimum(low) → green OBJ_HLINE support at that low; ArrayMaximum(high) → red OBJ_HLINE resistance at that high; OBJ_TREND from extreme low (or high) to current low (or high) as upward/downward trendline with ray. Continuously delete/redraw so structural levels track the visible window.
data_needed: CopyLow/CopyHigh/CopyRates over visible bar count; ChartGetInteger(CHART_FIRST_VISIBLE_BAR); chart objects.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Any _Symbol/_Period; levels keyed to currently visible chart window.
why_new_for_mis: Viewport-relative auto S/R and swing-trendline geometry as a structural level sensor for MIS (not fixed lookback).
quote: we will share here a method to detect price levels then drawing an updated type of line

mechanism: Alligator: Jaw=SMMA(median,13,shift8), Teeth=SMMA(median,8,shift5), Lips=SMMA(median,5,shift3). Bullish regime when lips>teeth>jaws (lines stacked below price); bearish when lips<teeth<jaws (stacked above). Price weaving through the three lines → sideways/range. Premise: markets trend only ~15–30% of time, range ~70–85%.
why_new_for_mis: Three-line SMMA stack as an explicit trend-vs-range regime sensor with Fibonacci periods—core Bill Williams balance-line geometry for MIS.
quote: If the price is above lips, teeth, then jaws, we can say the trend is up. If the price is below lips, teeth, then jaws, we can say that the trend is down. If the price is moving through the three lines, we can say that we have a sideways.

mechanism: Bill Williams Fractals: upward fractal when middle of ≥5 consecutive bars has highest high with lower highs on both sides → arrow above (potential downside/resistance pivot); downward fractal when middle has lowest low with higher lows on sides → arrow below (potential upside/support pivot). Sense latest non-EMPTY UPPER_LINE / LOWER_LINE fractal prices as swing high/low levels; optional gate with EMA(50) or Alligator stack.
data_needed: iFractals; UPPER_LINE and LOWER_LINE buffers (offset ~2); EMPTY_VALUE handling; optional MA/Alligator.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Any _Symbol/_Period; classical 5-bar pattern; EMA 50 and Alligator 13/8/5 in combo strategies.
why_new_for_mis: Pattern-confirmed local extrema as discrete swing-structure sensors for MIS support/resistance and reversal timing.
quote: The Fractals indicator needs a specific pattern of the price action to be formed on the chart in both directions up or down.

mechanism: Gator Oscillator = absolute divergence of Alligator balance lines (up histogram above zero, down below). Bar color: green if |bar| > prior, red if shrinking. Phases: both bars red → Sleeping (range); both green → Eating (trend continuation); green after red → Awakening (trend birth/entry); red after green → Sated (trend exhaustion/exit). Implemented by comparing current and two prior up/down Gator buffer values.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Any _Symbol/_Period; Alligator-linked 13/8/5 SMMA median; optional EMA(13) with double-green/double-red.
why_new_for_mis: Named four-phase lifecycle of trend (sleep→awaken→eat→sate) from Alligator line convergence/divergence—richer regime+change vocabulary than binary trend/range.
quote: If we have both bars red, the status of the Gator will be a sleeping phase. If we have both bars green, it will be an eating phase.

mechanism: Murray/Gann: divide trading range into 8ths (octave). Major octave height from Table 1 by price scale; minor/baby octaves by recursive /8. Sense MMML/mMML/bMML horizontals; vertical time intervals 4/8/16/32/64/128/256 (often 16d stocks, 32d FX/commodities); 8×8 squares and +2/8 extended overbought/oversold squares; speed diagonals (esp. 8:8, 3:2, 4:1). Even levels stronger S/R; 3/8–5/8 = 'country of happiness' (avoid); reversal probability rises with distance traveled in mMML units.
data_needed: Period high/low range; octave base from Table 1; horizontal 1/8…8/8; vertical rhythm from chosen origin; optional Fibo arcs for conflict circles at 2/8,4/8,6/8 intersections.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: USDJPY monthly worked examples; FX/commodities 32-day verticals; stocks/options 16d; mutual funds 64d; multi-octave from months down to intraday.
why_new_for_mis: Octave price+time lattice and speed-line geometry as a multi-scale structural regime map—far beyond single S/R lines.
quote: Horizontal levels are obtained by dividing the trading range into 8 parts.

mechanism: Conflict circles (Fibo Arcs) at intersections of 2/8,4/8,6/8 vertical×horizontal inside the main square: if price stays flat it avoids the innermost circle; active trend breaks into/touches the center—significant at all scales. Companion: if candle[1] volume changes ≥25% vs candle[2], mark red dot above (volume up) or blue below (volume down) as event-warning liquidity spike.
data_needed: Murray square geometry; Fibo Arcs scale so unit circle touches adjacent verticals; tick/real volume of bars [1] and [2]; ≥25% relative change threshold.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: USDJPY monthly conflict-circle demos; Volume-Murray.mq5 attached; per-timeframe arcs (scale not auto-recalculated across TFs).
why_new_for_mis: Geometric conflict-zone touch plus abrupt volume-change dots as liquidity/event sensors co-located on Murray structure.
quote: If the volume of the candle number [1] has changed dramatically (by 25% or more) in any direction compared to the candle [2], we are likely to expect important events in the near future

mechanism: Owl Full Fractals: 5 bars left + 2 right of extreme (vs classic 2+2). Valable ZigZag holds direction while fractal highs/lows advance with trend; reverses only when close breaks prior opposite fractal. Fibo grid 0–100 between first opposite fractals after ZZ turn; entries at 38.2/50/61.8, TP 161.8. Elder Triple Screen: require Valable ZZ same direction on trade TF, ×4, and ×16 (e.g. M15/H1/H4); Dead zone (red) when H1 direction ≠ H4—no trade. Optional slope channel + Fibo fan for early reverse.
data_needed: Full Fractals (FrBarsLeft=5, FrBarsRight=2); Valable ZigZag state; multi-TF ZZ directions; Fibo levels from fractal pair; channel/fan optional.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Any market/exchange claimed; example Triple Screen M15+H1+H4; commodities/stocks favor 50% Fibo entry.
why_new_for_mis: Asymmetric fractal + sticky ZigZag trend lock plus explicit multi-TF disagreement dead-zone as a tradeable regime filter for MIS.
quote: A dead zone is formed when the movement on H1 is different from that on H4.

mechanism: Bernoulli moral expectation / expected-utility sizing and Krichevsky–Trofimov shifted win-probability for lot/SL/TP—capital-relative risk math, not a market-state sensor. After full read: no regime/vol/liquidity/sequence sensing of the market itself.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H1 2021–2022 demo EA; simulated trades.
why_new_for_mis: Not applicable—money-management utility, not market sensing.
quote: in any game, it is necessary to maximize not the expected payoff, but its utility for the player

mechanism: Bill Williams Market Facilitation Index MFI=(High−Low)/Volume. Four states from co-movement of MFI and volume vs prior bar: Green—MFI↑ and vol↑ (participants interested / good entry); Fade—MFI↓ and vol↓ (disinterest / exit); Fake—MFI↑ and vol↓ (move not volume-supported / false-breakout risk); Squat—MFI↓ and vol↑ (balance / battleground). Optional: green + close vs SMA(10) for sided entries.
data_needed: iBWMFI(VOLUME_TICK or REAL); iVolumes; current and previous MFI and volume; optional iMA(10,SMA,CLOSE).
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Any _Symbol/_Period; tick or real volume; SMA 10 in strategy three.
why_new_for_mis: Joint price-range efficiency × volume state machine (green/fade/fake/squat) as a discrete liquidity/participation sensor—stronger than raw volume alone.
quote: If the BW MFI and volume increase, it indicates as the market participants are interested in this financial instrument.
